exposure: Study period (Ulm Birth Cohort Study (UBCS) in 2000 vs Ulm SPATZ Health Study (SPATZ) in 2012)
outcome: n-6 and n-3 long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acid (LCPUFA) intake
cohort: Lactating women recruited from the general population in Ulm, Germany (UBCS: n=567, SPATZ: n=458)
finding: Human milk fatty acid profiles differed significantly between the two cohorts, with the more recent cohort (SPATZ) showing higher levels of vegetable oil intake and lower intakes of trans-fatty acids and SFAs, potentially reflecting changes in maternal dietary habits.
